findings.highlight: She’s rejecting everything. Her own body, covered in Tohsaka’s blood, her darkened self, the pillar connected to her.
findings.evidenceJa: こうしている自分。遠坂の血に濡れた自分、黒く染まった自分、自分に繋がったあの黒い影を
findings.governingReading: Sakura rejects her present self, the self stained with Rin’s blood, the self dyed black, and the black shadow joined to her.
findings.explanation: The English collapses a structured inventory of hated selves and substitutes a pillar for the connected black shadow.

findings.highlight: She’s cursing everything with all her might.
findings.evidenceJa: 半狂乱になりながら、全力で憎んでいる。
findings.governingReading: Half frantic, Sakura hates all of it with everything she has.
findings.explanation: The English removes her near-frenzied mental state and changes hatred into generic cursing.

findings.highlight: You always told me not to lose
findings.evidenceJa: ダメだって、負けるなって姉さんはずっと言ってくれてたのに
findings.governingReading: Nee-san kept telling me both “No” and “Don’t lose.”
findings.explanation: One half of Rin’s repeated admonition disappears, narrowing what Sakura remembers receiving from her.

findings.highlight: The black Command Spell’s binding Sakura’s body.
findings.evidenceJa: 全身を覆った黒い令呪
findings.governingReading: The black Command Spells covering Sakura’s entire body bind her.
findings.explanation: The English changes the body-covering plural marks into one Command Spell and weakens their extent.

findings.highlight: Sakura’s necessary as a host for the shadow.
findings.evidenceJa: あの影にとって、桜は必要な本体だ。
findings.governingReading: For the shadow, Sakura is the necessary main body or core body.
findings.explanation: The English replaces the shadow’s principal-body relation with the looser idea of a host.

findings.highlight: Sakura’s being torn apart by both the shadow and her own guilty conscience.
findings.evidenceJa: 桜は自分を殺そうとする自責と、それをさせまいとする影によって切り刻まれている。
findings.governingReading: Sakura is cut apart between the self-reproach driving her to kill herself and the shadow preventing her from doing so.
findings.explanation: The English names two pressures but removes their opposed actions, which explain why Sakura is trapped.

findings.highlight: Sakura regained her sanity.
findings.evidenceJa: 桜の憑き物は落ちている。
findings.governingReading: The possessing influence has fallen away from Sakura.
findings.explanation: The English makes Sakura herself insane and newly sane instead of describing the external possession as lifted.

findings.highlight: scolded her
findings.evidenceJa: ぱかん、と叩いていたら
findings.governingReading: if I had given her a light pakan smack
findings.explanation: The English removes the small physical and comic mechanism Shirou imagines could have broken the spiral.

findings.highlight: She’s still breathing.
findings.evidenceJa: かろうじて呼吸をしている。
findings.governingReading: She is barely managing to breathe.
findings.explanation: The English preserves survival but removes how close Rin is to death.

findings.highlight: He’s not alive yet
findings.evidenceJa: まだ生まれてもないクセに
findings.governingReading: Though it has not even been born yet
findings.explanation: The English changes unborn status into nonlife and assigns the entity a male gender absent here.

findings.highlight: It should’ve cut through my neck
findings.evidenceJa: 俺の首をかっ飛ばしたソレ
findings.governingReading: the strike that ordinarily would have blown Shirou’s neck or head off
findings.explanation: The English weakens a decapitating impact into a cut through the neck.

findings.highlight: Sakura’s scream made it miss.
findings.evidenceJa: 桜の叫びで、軌道を変えてくれたようだ。
findings.governingReading: Sakura’s scream seems to have made it change trajectory.
findings.explanation: The English removes Sakura’s concrete redirection of the attack.

findings.highlight: the pain of the shadow swallowing her
findings.evidenceJa: 自身を蝕む影の痛み
findings.governingReading: the pain of the shadow eating away at her
findings.explanation: The English changes ongoing bodily erosion into the broader image of being swallowed.

findings.highlight: She’s crying from frustration because she can’t suppress herself.
findings.evidenceJa: あの影に操られるしかない自分が悔しくて泣いている。
findings.governingReading: She cries from frustration that she cannot suppress herself and can only be manipulated by that shadow.
findings.explanation: The English omits the second and more coercive half of Sakura’s reason for crying.

findings.highlight: I’ll, I’ll die here! I can die by myself…!
findings.evidenceJa: ちゃんと、ちゃんとここで死にますから、ひとりでもちゃんと死にますから
findings.governingReading: I will die properly here—properly; even alone, I will die properly.
findings.explanation: The English keeps the death wish but loses the repeated insistence on doing it properly, a key part of Sakura’s self-punitive resolve.

findings.highlight: I shouldn’t live.
findings.evidenceJa: わたしは、生きてちゃいけない人間だった
findings.governingReading: I was the kind of person who must not be allowed to live.
findings.explanation: The English reduces Sakura’s categorical judgment of what sort of person she was into a present personal recommendation.

findings.highlight: he’s not going to let me go.
findings.evidenceJa: この子もわたしを放してくれない。
findings.governingReading: This child will not let me go either.
findings.explanation: The English resolves Sakura’s childlike guarded referent as male without support in the line.

findings.highlight: Andeven if I do go back…
findings.evidenceJa: それにもし、戻れた、ところで
findings.governingReading: And even if I could go back…
findings.explanation: A missing space visibly joins two English words.

findings.highlight: WhatWhat do you want me to do…!?
findings.evidenceJa: そんなそんな人間にどうしろっていうんです
findings.governingReading: What do you expect someone like that to do?
findings.explanation: A duplicated English word visibly corrupts the question.

findings.highlight: She can’t back out now.
findings.evidenceJa: 後戻りの出来ない道。
findings.governingReading: A road from which there is no return.
findings.explanation: The English turns an irreversible condition into the more voluntary idea of backing out at the present moment.

findings.highlight: those actions will haunt her forever.
findings.evidenceJa: 多くの人の命を奪った咎は、桜の心に在り続けるだろう。
findings.governingReading: The guilt or blame for taking many lives will remain in Sakura’s heart.
findings.explanation: The English generalizes the lives taken into “actions” and removes their continuing location in Sakura’s heart.

findings.highlight: the darkness will remain within her.
findings.evidenceJa: 桜の中には昏い影が残ったままだ。
findings.governingReading: A dark shadow will remain inside Sakura.
findings.explanation: The English removes the recurring shadow image and substitutes abstract darkness.

findings.highlight: There are things I have to tell her.
findings.evidenceJa: 言わなくちゃいけない言葉を、まだ口にできるうちに、桜を。
findings.governingReading: Before he loses the ability to speak the necessary words, Shirou must reach Sakura—the source breaks off on her name.
findings.explanation: The English removes the closing window in which Shirou can still speak and smooths away the urgent broken object fragment.

findings.highlight: The shadows lance toward my chest, shoulder, left leg, and stomach.
findings.evidenceJa: 肩と胸、右足と腹に影が突き刺さる。
findings.governingReading: The shadows strike his shoulder, chest, right leg, and abdomen.
findings.explanation: The English puts the leg strike on the wrong side.

findings.highlight: I’ll protect you from everything.
findings.evidenceJa: これから桜に問われる全てのコトから桜を守るよ。
findings.governingReading: I will protect Sakura from everything she will be called to answer for from now on.
findings.explanation: The English removes the future moral and social accountability that defines what Shirou promises to protect Sakura from.

findings.highlight: my ideal has always been to protect the one I love
findings.evidenceJa: 好きな相手を守り通す事を、ずっと理想に生きてきたんだから
findings.governingReading: I have always lived by the ideal of protecting the person I love all the way through.
findings.explanation: The English retains the ideal’s object but removes Shirou’s claim that he has lived by it and its endurance through completion.

findings.highlight: the dagger that breaks all contracts
findings.evidenceJa: 契約破りの短剣
findings.governingReading: the contract-breaking dagger
findings.explanation: The English turns the dagger’s epithet into an unrestricted claim that it breaks every contract.
